summary: The investable universe for nuclear fuel conversion and HALEU is unusually thin. The obvious public-market anchors are Centrus Energy for enrichment/HALEU, BWX Technologies for advanced nuclear components and fuel-fabrication adjacency, and Honeywell as the indirect owner of the only operating US uranium conversion facility through ConverDyn/Metropolis Works. The underfollowed lane is difficult because many of the most relevant assets are private or embedded inside diversified companies. Therefore, the highest-value Layer 1B expansion is not a broad list of uranium miners, but a narrow watchlist of direct, embedded, and speculative-shadow names where later diligence must verify revenue exposure, contract structure, customer dependence, licensing milestones, and whether HALEU economics are material enough to matter.
